subject: Next steps: Hosted API routing, rate profile & sandbox access
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearauthority.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-17T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: Hosted API routing, rate profile & sandbox access

Hi Oliver — great demo earlier, really appreciated the clarity on your intent to run NLU for document ingestion and live chat summarization. Quick recap and a few narrow asks so we can scope a smooth hosted evaluation: 

- Preferred evaluation mode: you mentioned wanting to start on Hosted API for velocity, with Dedicated or VPC later for compliance. Correct?
- Traffic snapshot: can you confirm typical prompt length distribution and peak qps during business hours? A sample CSV (timestamps + request size) would be ideal.
- SLOs: what latency p50/p95 targets matter for the chat path? You said ~200–300ms p95 in the call — confirm.
- Endpoints: do you want one chat endpoint plus a separate batch embeddings endpoint, or a single multi-purpose endpoint?

Attached: we included a short endpoint proposal (redwood-hosted-endpoint-proposal.pdf) and a quick example CSV template if you want to drop in a traffic sample. 

Next steps we can take on our side:
- Provision a sandbox with two endpoints (chat + embeddings) for a 1‑week evaluation.
- Pre-warm prefix cache on any conversational flows you send regularly to reduce token costs.
- Suggest an initial rate cap: 80 reqs/s per endpoint with token-based throttling; we can lower/higher after we see your sample.

If Hosted API still looks like the right first step, can you drop the traffic sample and confirm whether you need SOC 2 evidence right away or only once you move to Dedicated/VPC? Also share 2–3 time slots for a short sandbox handoff next week.

Cheers,

Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-hosted-endpoint-proposal.pdf (11KB)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearauthority.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: api-team@clearauthority.com
Date: 2028-05-17T18:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted API routing, rate profile & sandbox access

Thanks Mina — nice summary. Confirming a few points and dropping a quick traffic sample.

- Hosted first: yes, we'd like to pilot on Hosted API to validate latencies and correctness. Plan is to move to Dedicated or VPC in Q3 if the POC is successful.
- Traffic sample: attached (clear_authority_traffic_sample.csv). It's one week of production-like traffic from our dev cluster — mostly short prompts (average 60 tokens), occasional long retrieval calls (~600 tokens). Peak observed ~65 req/s; typical daytime 15–25 req/s.
- Latency target: our internal bar for the chat path is p95 < 350ms. For batch embedding jobs p95 can be up to 2s.
- Endpoints: please provision chat (streaming supported) and an embeddings batch endpoint. We will kick off single-endpoint testing first.

Compliance: we need SOC 2 report and an outline of data retention and deletion practices before we expand to dedicated capacity. For the Hosted pilot we need to understand what parts of our data are retained and for how long. Specific question: will prompts be stored in logs accessible to Redwood engineers by default?

Sandbox handoff: Tuesdays/Wednesdays 10–12 PT are best next week.

Cheers,
Oliver Grant
Head of Integrations, ClearAuthority
oliver.grant@clearauthority.com

Attachment: clear_authority_traffic_sample.csv (14KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearauthority.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted API routing, rate profile & sandbox access

Hi Oliver — looping in a short, practical proposal based on your sample. Thanks for the CSV — helpful. Key items we recommend for a Hosted pilot (fast, low friction):

1) Endpoint mapping
- /v1/chat (streaming): conversational flows, set streaming=true, max_tokens ~512
- /v1/embeddings-batch: async jobs for nightly vectorization (we'll provide job id callbacks)

2) Rate profile (initial caps we suggest for the sandbox)
- Chat endpoint: 80 req/s burstable to 120 for short windows; token-based backpressure at 120k tokens/min.
- Embeddings-batch: 8 concurrent jobs, each with 10k tokens/min budget.

3) Cost & cache knobs
- Enable prefix (KV) cache on chat history you expect to reuse — this can reduce tokens by ~20–40% depending on repetition.
- Suggested quantization model for test: redwood-compact-v2 (lower latency for chat).

4) Compliance and logs
- For Hosted pilots, logs/requests are retained for 30 days by default and are available to your org via the Console. Access by Redwood SREs is audited; we can provide SOC 2 evidence and a sanitized audit extract.
- If you require complete isolation of logs (no Redwood access), Dedicated or Private VPC is required.

5) Next operational steps
- We will provision a 7‑day sandbox with the endpoints above and preloaded prefix cache on repeated prompts (please point out the top 10 repeated prompts if you have them).
- I'll drop a short handoff runbook and a DocuSign for an evaluation order (no long-term commit) if that speeds provisioning.

Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-sandbox-handoff.md (4KB)
Link: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/CLRA-2028-001
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@clearauthority.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Hosted API routing, rate profile & sandbox access

Perfect — that plan lines up with our expectations. A couple quick clarifications before you provision: 

- We'll send the top-10 repeated prompts by EOD today so you can seed the prefix cache.
- SOC 2: we only need the report and a short note about engineer access for the pilot (not the full artifact yet).
- DocuSign: please send the evaluation order and we'll route it to procurement (no approvals required for the sandbox).
- Sandbox scheduling: Tuesday 2028-05-23 at 10:30 PT works for our team. Can Mina run the 30-minute handoff?

Thanks — excited to get started.

Oliver
Head of Integrations, ClearAuthority
